• Send bulky, low-priority items with grandmother's car: the older child's high chair, beach chairs/windbreak, buckets and spades. That single decision frees the most boot space of anything on this list.
• The Mountain Buggy is the constraint, not the suitcases — fold it and place it first so you're building luggage around a known shape, not fitting it in last.
• Swap hard suitcases for 2-3 soft duffels or packing cubes; they compress and wedge into the odd-shaped gaps a folded stroller and travel cot leave behind.

• Ask Floreal directly whether bed linen, towels, and a baby cot/travel cot can be rented on-site — many Belgian holiday parks offer this, and skipping the travel cot alone can free up a third of the usable trunk floor.

• Do a one-week grocery run near Wortegem/on arrival in Nieuwpoort (Carrefour, Colruyt) for nappies, wipes, and formula top-ups rather than packing the full week's supply — it's the single heaviest, bulkiest category on the list.
• Keep a small 'first hour' bag in the cabin (nappies, wipes, one change of clothes, a ready feed, dummy) so you're not digging through the packed trunk the moment you arrive or need a stop.
• Install the infant car seat before loading anything else, so you're not repositioning boot contents around it afterwards.

• With a 2-month-old, the realistic 'activities' are the beach, promenade, and dune walks — anything letting her sleep in the pram or ride in the carrier. Don't over-plan around her.
• The harbour boat trip, museums, and indoor playground work much better with a carrier than with the full-size Mountain Buggy.

• Since your oldest travels separately with grandmother and uncle, decide in advance which days you'll split (they take him to Sunparks/the indoor playground) versus days together as a full group (the farm, the beach, a family dinner).
• Early August is peak season on the coast — book ahead for the sit-down restaurants, especially Brasserie Sunbeach, La Marée, and Tiffanys.
